title: Training data model, week-1 baseline program generation & program management
steps:
TRAINING DATA MODEL (PRD §2, §4 memory, §5, §9, §11; docs/milestones.md M3). Read the M2 profile/goals/baselines model and services first and build on them.

Design a discipline-agnostic, extensible schema (drizzle migrations via pnpm db:generate) and services/repositories with zod validation for:
- Exercise library: a seeded catalogue (aim for 150+ well-chosen exercises across barbell, dumbbell, machine, cable, bodyweight, kettlebell, Olympic lifts, plyometrics, conditioning, mobility) with movement pattern (squat, hinge, horizontal/vertical push/pull, lunge, carry, rotation, olympic, plyo, conditioning…), primary/secondary muscles, equipment required, discipline tags, unilateral flag, skill level, default rep ranges, and substitution groups that preserve training intent. Seed via a committed, idempotent seed (migration or seed script run by migrate) — not ad-hoc inserts. Owner-created custom exercises supported.
- Programs → immutable program VERSIONS → cycles/blocks (phase type: baseline, accumulation, intensification, realization/peak, deload, taper, hypertrophy, marathon base/build/peak/taper, maintenance) → weeks → planned sessions (date, discipline, session type, order in day, estimated duration and load, status planned/completed/skipped/moved) → planned exercises with set prescriptions (sets, reps or rep range, target RPE, load prescription kind: absolute | percent_1rm | rpe_based | from_e1rm with value, rest seconds, tempo optional, notes) → planned running sessions with ordered segments (warmup, steady, interval, recovery, tempo, long, cooldown with distance/duration/pace range/HR zone/RPE targets and repeats) → planned other sessions (Muay Thai pads/sparring/technical/conditioning/class, mobility, S&C, custom) with duration, target RPE and custom metrics.
- Logged training (used by M4 — design it now so history queries are fast): completed workouts (linked to the planned session if any, started/finished, device-generated idempotency ids), set records (exercise, set index, weight + unit, reps, RPE, missed reps, flags warmup/extra/skipped, timestamps, client mutation id UNIQUE), running sessions with segments (distance, duration, pace, HR optional, RPE, notes), other sessions with custom metrics (jsonb with a validated shape), body-weight and recovery notes.
- Coaching memory foundations: programming decisions (what changed, why, who decided: owner | coach | rules, linked program version and affected entities, created_at), exercise preferences (explicit dislike / like with reason and source; situational substitutions are recorded on the session ONLY and never become preferences), AI recommendations/proposals (status proposed/accepted/rejected/applied — table only, M5 uses it), weekly and cycle reviews (tables only, M6 fills them).
- History is never overwritten: edits to planned programming create a NEW program version (copy-on-write of affected rows) with a decision record; logged training rows are append-only except explicit owner edits, which keep updated_at and an audit trail. Prove with integration tests.
- Indexes for the main history queries: exercise history by exercise ordered by time, last N performances of an exercise, PR lookup, weekly volume per muscle group, sessions by date range, running mileage by week, current program/week lookup. Add `pnpm db:explain`: seeds a realistic large dataset into a scratch database (2+ years: ~600 workouts, ~15k set records, ~400 runs) and prints EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) for each main query; commit the measured plans/timings in docs/performance.md (real numbers only) and fix any sequential scans on large tables.
- Domain functions (pure, unit-tested in src/lib/domain): e1RM from a set with reps+RPE (reuse M1's), best e1RM per exercise, weekly hard sets per muscle group, session load (sRPE × duration), running weekly mileage — these are reused by M4–M7.
- Integration tests (real Postgres): create profile → program → version → cycle → planned week → retrieve; exercise history queries; versioning never overwrites; concurrent disciplines (strength + running + Muay Thai) in one week; idempotent set-record insert (same client mutation id twice → one row).
- Docs: data model section (ER overview) in docs/architecture.md, ADR for the versioning strategy, docs/milestones.md status.

WEEK-1 BASELINE PROGRAM GENERATION (deterministic rules, NO LLM — the coach in M5 will call the same generator as a tool). Build src/lib/server/services/programming/ (pure domain logic in src/lib/domain where possible) that turns the owner's profile into a complete first program:
- Inputs: goals with priority ranking (event/general, dates), disciplines and experience, schedule & availability (days, preferred times, session length, fixed commitments such as Muay Thai classes), equipment, injuries/limitations/movements to avoid, exercise likes/dislikes, strength baselines (measured/estimated/blank), running ability, body/nutrition phase.
- Week 1 is a BASELINE ESTABLISHMENT week: when a lift's 1RM is unknown, prescribe RPE-based working sets (e.g. work up to a set of 5 @ RPE 7, then back-off sets) with clear instructions to record weight/reps/RPE so e1RM can be estimated; when known (measured or estimated), use conservative percentages; never treat estimated as measured; avoid aggressive loading in week 1.
- Subsequent weeks of the first block (e.g. 3 accumulation weeks + deload, or as appropriate to goals/event dates) with progression rules expressed as data (load/RPE/volume targets) so M4/M6 can adapt them.
- Session placement across the available days with concurrent-training rules: fixed commitments (Muay Thai classes) are placed first; no heavy lower-body strength the day before hard Muay Thai/sparring or a long run; intervals not right after a very demanding day; hard days separated where possible; goal priority decides conflicts; session length respected (exercise count/sets fit the time).
- Exercise selection: goal- and discipline-appropriate splits (strength, hypertrophy, general athletic), equipment-available only, injuries/movements-to-avoid excluded, disliked exercises never prescribed, likes preferred; balanced movement patterns and weekly hard sets per muscle group within sensible ranges for the goal.
- Running: easy runs, a long run, and quality sessions only as experience/goals warrant; weekly volume derived from current volume with conservative progression; marathon/half goals with an event date produce a block structure leading toward it (detailed periodisation is M7 — keep the hooks).
- Every non-trivial choice writes a programming decision with a human-readable rationale (the 'why').
- Deterministic: same profile → same program (seeded tie-breaks); unit tests for each rule and scenario tests for: strength-only beginner with all 1RMs blank; powerlifter with measured 1RMs; hybrid athlete (strength + marathon + Muay Thai Tue/Thu) with conflicts; injured shoulder avoiding overhead pressing; minimal equipment (dumbbells only).

PROGRAM MANAGEMENT UI (premium, iPhone-first, dark-first; reuse/extend the design system; no generic tables). Build on M2's authenticated app and onboarding:
- After onboarding, Today shows a 'Build my program' moment that runs the generator and presents the result with its rationale (what week 1 is for and why); confirming creates program version 1.
- Train tab: current program → cycle/block → week view (horizontal day strip/calendar showing strength, running and Muay Thai sessions with discipline colours used sparingly) → planned session detail (exercises with sets × reps @ RPE/load prescription and rest, running segments, Muay Thai session details), clearly marking week 1 as baseline establishment with instructions.
- Owner edits: move a session to another day, swap an exercise for an alternative from its substitution group (explicit 'never prescribe this again' option creates a persistent dislike; a one-off swap does not), adjust a prescription, skip a planned session. Each edit creates a new program version with a decision record; a 'History' view lists versions and decisions with their why, and older versions remain viewable.
- Today shows today's planned session(s) and what's next this week; empty/rest-day states designed.
- Accessibility (axe, both themes), performance budgets (route JS ≤ 60 KB gzip; lazy-load heavy views), no layout shift, view transitions consistent with the shell.
- Playwright (authenticated via the M2 fixture): complete onboarding with every 1RM blank → generate week-1 baseline program → the planned week shows strength + running + Muay Thai sessions on sensible days → open a session and see RPE-based baseline prescriptions → move a session and swap an exercise → version history shows both changes with rationale → reload persists; a second scenario with measured 1RMs shows percentage-based loads. Save screenshots of every new screen for review.
- Integration: create profile → generate program → planned week → retrieve; edits create versions; history intact. Update docs (architecture data model, milestones, testing) and record EXPLAIN evidence in the PR body later (summarise measured plans in your summary).
acceptance: Discipline-agnostic schema with committed migrations covers exercises (movement patterns, muscles, equipment, substitution groups; 150+ seeded idempotently), programs → immutable versions → cycles/blocks → weeks → planned sessions → set prescriptions, running sessions with segments, other sessions with custom metrics, logged workouts/set records (unique client mutation ids), programming decisions with rationale, preferences, recommendations and review tables.

New programming never overwrites history: edits create new program versions with decision records and older versions remain readable; logged training is append-only except audited owner edits — proven by integration tests against real Postgres.

Integration tests: create profile → generate program → planned week → retrieve; exercise history and last-performance queries; idempotent set-record insert; a single week containing strength, running and Muay Thai sessions.

Indexes exist for the main history queries and `pnpm db:explain` on a realistic 2-year dataset shows index usage (no sequential scans on large tables) with real EXPLAIN ANALYZE timings recorded in docs/performance.md.

Week-1 baseline generation is deterministic and rule-based: blank 1RMs → RPE-based baseline sets with recording instructions; known 1RMs → conservative percentages (estimated never treated as measured); equipment, injuries/movements to avoid and dislikes respected; fixed commitments placed first and concurrent-training placement rules applied; every significant choice has a recorded rationale — covered by unit and scenario tests (beginner/blank, powerlifter/measured, hybrid strength+marathon+Muay Thai, injured shoulder, dumbbells only).

Playwright: authenticated owner completes onboarding with every 1RM blank, generates the week-1 baseline program, sees strength + running + Muay Thai in the planned week, opens a session with RPE-based prescriptions, moves a session and swaps an exercise, sees both in version history with rationale, and everything persists across reload.
A one-off exercise swap does not create a persistent preference, while an explicit 'never prescribe again' does (tested at the service level and in the UI).

New screens (build-my-program, Train week view, session detail, edit flows, history) are premium and intentional on an iPhone viewport with designed empty/rest-day/loading/error states; axe zero violations in dark and light; route JS ≤ 60 KB gzip; perf e2e guard green.
Pure domain functions for e1RM (with RPE), weekly hard sets per muscle group, session load and running mileage are unit-tested and documented for reuse by later milestones.

All gates pass locally (check, lint, unit, integration, both builds, budgets, full e2e incl. perf project) and docs are updated (data model, versioning ADR, milestones, testing); all work committed on feat/m3-training-model with Conventional Commits.
